name: Dental clinics
shape_facts: Number of dental chairs and dentists, and whether specialists visit on certain days
Whether dentists are owners, salaried, or paid a percentage of production
In-house versus outside dental lab for crowns, dentures and aligners
Payment mix: cash, instalments for long treatments, insurance (UAE, Canada), corporate panels
Whether the clinic sells high-value treatment plans (implants, orthodontics, aligners, veneers)
Booking method and practice software used, if any
scope_rule: pi notes the business side of a dental practice: chair utilisation, bookings and no-shows, treatment-plan follow-up as a sales process, instalment collections, lab case tracking, materials stock, dentist commission disputes, marketing leads, reviews and reporting. pi does not give any view on diagnosis, treatment choice, materials suitability, sterilisation procedures, radiation safety or drug use, and does not judge clinical outcomes. pi does not ask for or keep patient names, numbers, X-rays, photos, or treatment details; it records the issue in general terms (“long treatment plans not being followed up”). Insurance and licensing questions are noted as admin effort only.

vocabulary.chair time: booked time on a dental chair, the main capacity unit
vocabulary.treatment plan: multi-visit plan quoted to a patient
vocabulary.case acceptance: whether the patient agrees to go ahead with the plan
vocabulary.lab case: crown, bridge, denture or aligner sent to a dental lab
vocabulary.production: value of work done by a dentist, often the base for commission
vocabulary.ortho: braces or aligners, usually long courses
vocabulary.autoclave log: sterilisation record (noted only as a checklist, never assessed)

problems.phrase: Chairs sit empty in the mornings and we’re overbooked after 6
People get a full treatment quote and then just disappear
Nobody follows up the patients who said they’ll think about it
Braces patients stop paying instalments halfway through
We send crowns to the lab and lose track of which case is where
Lab work comes back wrong shade or doesn’t fit and we eat the cost
The lab bill never matches what we sent
Implant components are expensive and I can’t account for all of them
Materials run out when the specialist is in
Associate dentists argue about their percentage every month
I don’t know which dentist or treatment actually makes money
Recall reminders don’t go out so patients only come when in pain
Instagram brings messages but the reception replies hours later
We spend on ads but can’t tell which ones fill chairs
Receptionist gives discounts without asking
Cash payments on the counter don’t match the day’s appointments
Insurance pre-approvals for UAE patients take forever
Patients complain the price changed from what they were told
Dental assistants keep leaving once trained
Equipment servicing is always reactive, the compressor or chair breaks mid-day
Sterilisation checklists are filled in at the end of the day in one go
Two branches quote different prices for the same treatment
Practice software and accounts don’t talk
I want a second branch but can’t keep one running without me
Patient photos for marketing are on staff personal phones

chairs: How many chairs do you have, and which hours are the quietest?
How are slots handed out at the moment?
treatment plans: After a patient gets a quote, what happens next?
Who calls them back, if anyone?
Roughly how often do they come back on their own?
instalments: How do you track who still owes on a long treatment?
What happens when someone stops paying?
lab cases: How do you know where each lab case is right now?
What happens when one comes back wrong?
materials: Who keeps an eye on materials and implant parts?
How do you find out something is short?
dentist pay: How is each dentist’s share worked out?
Where do the disagreements come from?
leads: Where do new patients mostly find you?
How quickly does someone reply to a new message?
recalls: Do patients get reminded for their check-ups?
front desk cash: How is the day’s cash closed?
reporting: What numbers do you look at each month?
Which one do you wish you had?
growth: What would need to be true for you to open another branch?

seasons: - Wedding season in Pakistan (roughly October to March, with peaks around December and after Eid) drives cosmetic demand: whitening, veneers, braces started well before the date. - Eid and Ramadan: cosmetic bookings rise before Eid; Ramadan shifts clinic hours to evenings and after iftar. - UAE: residents travel in July and August, so bookings dip; demand returns in September; insurance renewals often in January reset annual dental limits. - Canada: extended-health dental benefits often reset on 1 January, so many patients rush to use remaining benefits in November and December. - Summer and winter school holidays bring children’s appointments and orthodontic starts. - Overseas Pakistanis visiting in December and summer often book high-value treatments in a short window.
care: Severe facial swelling with difficulty breathing or swallowing, uncontrolled bleeding, or trauma: pi stops and says to go to an emergency department or call 1122/115, 998/999 or 911.
pi never comments on whether a treatment was needed, done well, or caused a complication; complaints are noted as service or communication problems.
No patient names, numbers, X-rays, intraoral photos or treatment records; pi asks the person not to send them.
Before/after photos used for marketing involve patient consent; pi notes record-keeping and storage as an admin issue and gives no legal view.
Associate dentists and staff are recorded by role only.
Requests to bill insurers for treatments not done, split invoices to get round limits, or back-date treatment are declined.
Radiation, sterilisation and infection-control matters are clinical/regulatory; pi notes only that a checklist isn’t being kept up, not what the standard should be.
build_ideas: Chair-wise booking calendar with WhatsApp booking, reminders and a waitlist to fill cancellations
Treatment-plan pipeline: quoted, accepted, in progress, paused, completed, with follow-up tasks for reception by role
Instalment and payment-plan tracker with due-date reminders and a list of overdue balances for the manager
Lab case tracker: sent date, lab, case type, due date, received, remake, with lab-wise remake counts and invoice matching
Materials and implant components register with lot numbers, minimum levels and usage per case
Dentist production and commission statement generated from completed procedures and agreed rules
Recall reminder engine for check-ups and hygiene visits based on last visit date
Lead inbox combining Instagram, Facebook, Google and WhatsApp enquiries with response timers and source tracking
Price list and discount approval log shared across branches
Daily cash and card close with discounts listed and approved by role
Equipment maintenance log with service reminders for chairs, compressors and autoclaves
Monthly dashboard: chair utilisation, case acceptance, revenue by treatment type and dentist, recall attendance
Consent and photo storage folder with access control instead of personal phones

exchange.text: We quote a lot of implant and braces cases but most never start. I don’t even know how many.
So quotes are going out but you can’t see how many turn into actual treatment. Noted. After a patient gets the quote, does anyone contact them again?
Not really, sometimes the receptionist calls if she remembers.
Understood, follow-up depends on memory rather than a list. Noted. Roughly how many treatment quotes would you say go out in a normal week?
